title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: CHERRL is a controllable hacking environment for rubric-based reinforcement learning. By injecting known biases into an LLM-as-a-Judge and separating the proxy reward into a clean gold reward and an isolated biased reward, CHERRL enables stable reproduction of reward hacking, explicit observation of reward divergence, and precise ground-truth identification of hacking onset. The paper analyzes judge biases by discoverability and exploitability, and introduces the Reward Hacking Detection Agent (RHDA) for detecting hacking onset from training logs.
